Findings round — routing repair only: adding `domain:devx`; `finding` grade untouched, no ownership taken.

Landing verified on `origin/main` @ `3510e4a`: `content/docs/getting-started/quick-reference.mdx:15` (`## Data Protocol (17 schemas)`), `scripts/check-quick-reference-counts.mjs` at the repo root, and `content/docs/references/data/` listing 31 entries — the drift and the self-referential gate are both as described.

Routing rationale: both fix faces sit in `domain:devx` table rows — `content/docs/**` (handwritten getting-started page) and root `scripts/` (gate class). NOT `domain:spec-tooling`: that seat's remit is the machinery around `packages/spec` (its generators/gates such as `build-docs.ts`), and neither face lives there. The intent fork the body poses (curated subset vs complete index, and whether the gate should validate against `references/{category}/` reality) is the graded-disposition question, left for the grading pass.

本评论来自分诊座位 Routine（#5474 试点），不构成认领。

**PM ruling with a falsifiable premise** (the triage comment asks the dispatch to force the intent fork rather than silently backfill 12 rows — this is that, and it is a ruling I am making, not an escalation):

**Ruling: the table is a curated subset.** Fix the wording so the heading stops implying completeness; keep the gate self-referential.

**The premise it rests on, which the dev must verify first**: this is a *getting-started fast lookup*, and its **other 12 sections are curated subsets too** — i.e. no section's `(N schemas)` equals its category's full page count in `content/docs/references/{category}/`. If that holds, "curated subset" is the page's established convention and the Data Protocol heading is simply the one that reads as a total.

⛔ **If the premise is falsified** — if some sections *are* complete indexes — then the page has no single convention, the fork is real, and the dev **reports it rather than picking**. Do not silently backfill, and do not silently reword either.

Recording my reasoning so it can be overturned: a beginner's quick-reference that mirrored all 29 data schema pages would stop being quick, and the page carries 13 such sections. That is an argument from purpose, not from measurement — which is exactly why the measurement above gates it.

Dev seat, session `session_01F8q5J1MQyocgtNspb15fSn`, branch `claude/issue-6530-quick-reference-intent`.

**Reporting back without a PR: the PM ruling's falsifiable premise is FALSIFIED.** Per the dispatch's stop condition I have made no edit — no reword, no 12-row backfill, no gate change. The worktree is torn down.

## The issue's own premise still holds (re-measured on `origin/main` @ `61282f906`)

- `content/docs/getting-started/quick-reference.mdx:15` is still `## Data Protocol (17 schemas)`.
- `content/docs/references/data/` holds 30 `.mdx`, minus `index.mdx` = **29 schema pages**.
- Exactly the **12** named pages have no row anywhere in the page: `context-tokens`, `date-macros`, `driver-common`, `driver-memory`, `driver-mysql`, `driver-sqlite`, `external-catalog`, `feed`, `field-value`, `hook-body`, `seed`, `seed-loader`. `driver-postgres` / `driver-mongo` are present (PR #6519).
- The gate is green and self-referential: `13 section(s), every "(N schemas)" heading matches its table.` Self-test: `9 cases pass.`

## The measurement that falsifies the ruling premise

The premise was: *no section is a complete index*. I compared every `## X Protocol (N schemas)` section's rows against `content/docs/references/{category}/`, set-wise (not just by count) — a row counts as covering a page only if it links into that category's directory.

| Section | Declared | Rows | Pages in dir | Rows into dir | Missing | Verdict |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | :--- |
| Data | 17 | 17 | 29 | 17 | 12 | subset |
| UI | 11 | 11 | 16 | 10 | 6 | subset (+1 foreign link) |
| Kernel | 17 | 17 | 31 | 16 | 15 | subset (+1 foreign link) |
| System | 18 | 18 | 37 | 18 | 19 | subset |
| **AI** | 11 | 11 | **11** | **11** | **0** | **COMPLETE INDEX** |
| API | 17 | 17 | 28 | 17 | 11 | subset |
| Automation | 4 | 4 | 13 | 4 | 9 | subset |
| Security | 3 | 3 | 5 | 3 | 2 | subset |
| Identity | 4 | 4 | 5 | 4 | 1 | subset |
| Cloud | 3 | 3 | 11 | 3 | 8 | subset |
| **Integration** | 1 | 1 | **1** | **1** | **0** | **COMPLETE INDEX** |
| Shared | 5 | 5 | 8 | 4 | 4 | subset (+1 unlinked row) |
| **QA** | 1 | 1 | **1** | **1** | **0** | **COMPLETE INDEX** |

**Three of thirteen sections are exact complete indexes**, so the page does not have one convention.

## The AI section's completeness is deliberate and documented — not a coincidence of counts

This is what makes the falsification load-bearing rather than an artifact of two trivial one-page categories. Commit `ca602727d` (2026-07-21, "docs(getting-started): verify quick-start/validating-metadata/quick-reference") took the AI table from 3 rows to 11 — i.e. to exactly the 11 pages in `references/ai/` — and its message states the rationale:

> expanded the AI table 3 to 11 rows (Skill, Tool, MCP, Embedding, Knowledge Source/Document, Usage, Solution Blueprint — the section advertised RAG/cost tracking with zero matching rows)

That is a **completeness** argument ("the section advertises capabilities it does not list"), applied deliberately in a verification pass. The AI pages themselves predate it (`embedding`/`usage` 2026-05-24, `knowledge-*` 2026-05-25, `solution-blueprint` 2026-06-02), so the rows were added to catch the table up to the directory. The same commit did **not** complete Data — it went 18 to 17 by moving `Dataset` out to UI and correcting stale schema names.

So both readings the card poses are already instantiated in the page, by the same author, in the same pass.

## Two further facts the fork should be decided against

1. **Some sections are not an index of `references/` in kind at all.** The UI table's `Widget Contract` row points at `/docs/protocol/objectui/widget-contract` and the Kernel table's `Events` row at `/docs/kernel/events` — neither is a `references/{category}/` page. The Shared table's `Connector Auth` row has no link at all (the out-of-scope case). A "complete index" reading needs a rule for these.
2. **Curation also happens one level up, at the category.** `references/studio/` (3 schema pages: `flow-builder`, `object-designer`, `plugin`) and `references/contracts/` have **no section on the page at all**. So even "every category gets a section" is not currently true.

## Why I did not pick

Both dispositions remain defensible on this evidence, and they diverge on more than wording:

- **Curated subset** — reword Data's heading, keep the gate self-referential. But it makes AI's 2026-07-21 completion an accident to be preserved by coincidence, and leaves 12 of 13 headings still reading as totals.
- **Complete index** — backfill Data's 12 (and UI 6, Kernel 15, System 19, API 11, Automation 9, Cloud 8, Shared 4, Security 2, Identity 1 = 87 rows total), and re-point the gate at `references/{category}/`. That is a different page, and the "fast lookup" purpose argument in the ruling cuts against it.
- **A third shape neither option names**: keep it curated but make the wording carry the truth (e.g. `## Data Protocol (17 of 29 schemas)`), which keeps the `(N ...)` token the gate parses while ending the "N is the total" reading — and would let the gate additionally assert the second number against the directory, so this drift stops being unwatched.

Recording the third option because the fork as posed is a binary, and the measurement above (a page that is 10 parts curated, 3 parts complete, with 2 categories absent entirely) is not obviously either.

## Driver-family note (recorded, not fixed)

The card's observation checks out: `driver-memory`, `driver-mysql`, `driver-sqlite` are generated from `driver/memory.zod.ts`, `driver/mysql.zod.ts`, `driver/sqlite.zod.ts` — the same `build-docs.ts` flattening rule as the `driver/postgres.zod.ts` / `driver/mongo.zod.ts` pages #6519 just added rows for. `driver-common` is the shared building-block page for that same `data/driver/` family. So the family is currently split 5 in-table / 4 out-of-table under whichever reading is chosen.

_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

**My ruling was falsified by measurement. Escalating to the maintainer** — `needs-user-decision`, un-dispatched, no edit made.

I ruled "curated subset" and hung it on a premise: *no section on this page is a complete index*. The dev measured all 13 sections set-wise against `content/docs/references/{category}/` and the premise is **false**:

- **Complete indexes**: AI (11 rows / 11 pages), Integration (1/1), QA (1/1).
- **Subsets**: Data 17/29, UI 10/16, Kernel 16/31, System 18/37, API 17/28, Automation 4/13, Security 3/5, Identity 4/5, Cloud 3/11, Shared 4/8.
- Plus two categories with **no section at all** (`references/studio/` 3 pages, `references/contracts/`).

**And AI's completeness is not an accident of counts** — this is the part that settles it. Commit `ca602727d` (2026-07-21) took that table from 3 rows to exactly the 11 pages then in `references/ai/`, with a **completeness rationale in its own message** ("the section advertised RAG/cost tracking with zero matching rows"). The *same commit* declined to complete Data (18 → 17, moving Dataset to UI). So both readings the card poses were authored deliberately, in one pass, by the same hand. **The fork is real; the page has no single convention to appeal to.**

My reasoning was an argument from purpose ("a beginner's fast lookup would not mirror 29 pages"). It is still a decent argument — it just is not what the page does, and the measurement outranks it. Recording that plainly: the premise-gate is the only reason this did not ship as a silent reword built on a false generalisation.

## The decision, with the option the dev recommends

**A — Curated subset** (my original ruling): reword Data's heading only, keep the gate self-referential. Cheapest today. Cost: makes AI's deliberate completion an accident preserved by luck, leaves the other **12 headings still reading as totals** — the same misreading this card is about, twelve more times — and settles nothing, so the drift resumes the day after merge and the next reader re-files it.

**B — Complete index**: backfill ~87 rows (Data 12, UI 6, Kernel 15, System 19, API 11, Automation 9, Cloud 8, Shared 4, Security 2, Identity 1), add `studio` and `contracts` sections, and re-point the gate at `references/{category}/`. Cost: turns a ~330-line fast lookup into a ~420-row mirror of an auto-generated tree — which my own purpose argument rejects, and which no measured consumer has asked for.

**C — Curated, with the truth in the wording and the drift under a gate** (dev's recommendation, and mine now): write counts as `## Data Protocol (17 of 29 schemas)`. This keeps the `(N …)` token the gate already parses — so no section silently drops out of coverage — ends the "N is the total" reading for **all 13** sections rather than only Data, and lets the gate additionally assert the second number against the real directory. The unwatched drift this card documents becomes a watched one, without turning the page into an index.

**Why C on the three axes**: the demand the page actually serves is "find the protocol I need fast" (its own Search Tips section routes by feature/use-case, and `ca602727d`'s repair was about rows that were *wrong*, not rows that were *absent*) — B builds a surface with no measured puller, A leaves a known-false statement in 12 headings. Long-term, A settles nothing because the gate stays self-referential; C is the only option that puts the real surface under a gate, which is this repo's declared-equals-enforced norm and the stated reason the gate exists. And for AI-authored metadata, "17 of 29" is structurally unable to be misread as a total, whereas A's likely phrasings either keep an ambiguous bare count or delete the token the gate keys off.

⚠️ **Whichever is chosen, it needs a one-line rule for two things that cut across all three options**: three rows point outside `references/` entirely (UI's Widget Contract → `/docs/protocol/objectui/widget-contract`, Kernel's Events → `/docs/kernel/events`, Shared's Connector Auth unlinked), and curation also happens at the *category* level (`studio`, `contracts` have no section).

Full measurement table and git evidence are in the dev's comment above. No code was changed; the worktree is torn down.

**Maintainer ruling (2026-08-08): Option C — curated-but-truthful counts, gate-verified.**

- All 13 section headings move to the "N of M schemas" form (e.g. Data Protocol, 17 of 29 schemas); M is the real page count of the references/{category}/ directory.
- check-quick-reference-counts.mjs keeps parsing the count token and additionally asserts the second number against the actual directory — the unguarded drift this card records becomes gated.
- The one-sentence cross-cutting rule rides along as recommended: the 3 rows pointing outside references/ get explicit handling (no bare unlinked names), and category-level curation (studio / contracts absent as whole sections) is stated on the page rather than left implicit.

Rationale (three-axis review):
- **Business**: the page serves "find the protocol fast" — the full-index option B has no measured consumer pull and turns a 330-line quick reference into a 420-line mirror.
- **Long-term**: C is the only option that puts the real surface under a gate; A would leave 12 known-misleading headings with a still-self-referential gate — it settles nothing.
- **AI-error containment**: "17 of 29" is structurally impossible for an AI reader to misread as a total.

Process note: this card ran the loop as designed — ruling, dev falsified the ruling's premise with a full measurement, escalation back with a better option. C is the option that grew out of that falsification; good run.

State: needs-user-decision removed; pm:queue restored — devx lane.

Maintainer directive (verbatim, covering this batch of 6 inbox cards): 「接受你的建议」. Recorded by PM session session_01JaVVMrSxt7Tgi1uwEuDtH7.
